Victor Marx

Republican candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Colorado · Open seat

Ministry leader; founder of a faith-based organization; Marine Corps veteran

Victor Marx, 61, is a Marine Corps veteran and ministry leader who founded an organization that carries out missions abroad. He is running for public office for the first time. He beat Barb Kirkmeyer in the 2026 Colorado Republican gubernatorial primary to become the party's nominee, and George Markert is his lieutenant governor running mate.

Where Marx stands

Amendment 87 (graduated income tax)
Opposes Amendment 87. Says nearly doubling the top income tax rate would make other states more attractive than Colorado, not make Colorado more prosperous.
TABOR / Proposition NN and Proposition 137
Opposes Propositions NN and 137. Argues they would essentially erase TABOR refunds for the foreseeable future.
Medicaid
Says he would audit the agency before deciding on cuts, and would target waste, improper payments, administrative inefficiencies and unsustainable cost growth. Says more revenue should not end demands for accountability.
State budget / structural deficit
Proposes a review of agency spending, contracts, vacant positions and duplicative programs. Would make departments justify their spending and would rebid contracts competitively. Puts public safety, education, infrastructure and essential services first.
Housing and cost of living
Proposes faster residential permitting, a review of mandates that raise construction costs, more relief for seniors and more competition in property insurance. Would require cost-benefit analysis before new regulations.
Public safety
Supports law enforcement. Says he would focus resources on violent crime, fentanyl, trafficking and repeat offenders.
Government accountability
Proposes audits of executive agencies and a public dashboard showing state spending, contracts and agency performance.

Background

  • Served in the U.S. Marine Corps
  • Founded a faith-based organization that conducts missions abroad
  • First run for public office
  • Won the 2026 Republican gubernatorial primary over Barb Kirkmeyer
  • Chose George Markert as his running mate for lieutenant governor
